sources.entry: betterglobekey - Make macOS Globe key great again! [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/Serpentiel/betterglobekey) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: A macOS utility that reworks the Globe key so it cycles through your own ordered input sources, with double-press switching collections and Shift reversing direction.
summary.what_it_does: The tool replaces macOS's default Globe key behavior for switching input sources. A single press moves to the next input source in the current collection, and a double press moves to the next collection. Shift reverses either action. An on-screen HUD shows the new input source and its collection. Other keys such as Caps Lock or Right Command can also trigger switching, which helps on keyboards without a Globe key. Configuration is a YAML file at ~/.betterglobekey.yaml that reloads when changed, and the README mentions an optional companion app for editing it. The CLI includes `betterglobekey list` to show available input sources and `betterglobekey doctor` to check permissions and settings.
use_cases: Switch keyboard layouts quickly on macOS
Use Caps Lock or Right Command to change input source
Replace the default Globe key behavior
Group input sources into collections for everyday and occasional use
Switch input methods on keyboards without a Globe key
how_to_run: Write the configuration to ~/.betterglobekey.yaml (see README example with version: 2, trigger, and collections)
Set 'Press 🌐 key to' to 'Do Nothing' under System Settings > Keyboard
Run betterglobekey doctor to verify setup
notable: Two-level switching: single press cycles sources within a collection, double press cycles collections
Shift reverses direction for both sources and collections
Config file reloads automatically when saved
Works with non-Globe keys such as Caps Lock or Right Command
Includes a doctor command that checks Accessibility permission and Globe key settings
caveats: Requires Accessibility permission and changing the macOS 'Press 🌐 key to' setting to 'Do Nothing'
The README does not describe other platforms beyond macOS
The optional companion app is mentioned but not described in detail in the README
